_doc: Linux (`platform: linux`) entries for librendersystemvulkan.so of build 2000930 (the build the Windows
rendersystemvulkan.dll in the database is, ClientVersion 2000930). The module exports no `_ZTV` symbol for its
own classes, so the vtable is located by its complete-object destructor, which begins with `push rbp; lea
rax,[rip+vtable]` and stores the address point as the object's first qword, the way libengine2.json's
CRenderService is. VTLEN_CRenderDeviceVulkan is the `vtlen` scan of that table; sdkcheck.py compares it with the
Itanium vtable length of the generated IRenderDevice (LINUX_VT_PAIRS).
Nothing here has a `bridge` macro: the bridge gate covers the Windows entries only.

CRenderDeviceVulkan.via: librendersystemvulkan.so 0x5b0100: the complete-object destructor, which begins with push rbp, lea rax,[rip+vtable] (the CRenderDeviceVulkan vtable address point), stores it as the object's first qword and a secondary table (address point + 0x948) at +0x1120. No `_ZTV` symbol is exported for the class
CRenderDeviceVulkan.notes: IRenderDevice implementation (the RenderDevice003 interface), primary table, offset-to-top 0; the Windows build's table has 292 entries (s2sdk-types RE6 section 4)

VTLEN_CRenderDeviceVulkan.via: librendersystemvulkan.so address point 0x89d188: 295 .text slot pointers up to the next table's header
VTLEN_CRenderDeviceVulkan.notes: Itanium length of IRenderDevice's implementation, compared by sdkcheck.py with upstream's Itanium vtable length of IRenderDevice (255): the interface's 255 slots, then the two destructor entries and 35 virtuals of CRenderDeviceBase, then 3 of CRenderDeviceVulkan's own (RE6 section 4)
